Guideline: Start with useState for local values
Description: A value only one component reads belongs in that component's own state, not in a store.
Do: Keep the value next to the component that shows it.
Don't: Reach for a global store for a toggle or an input.

Description: A value computed from props or state needs no state of its own; storing it creates two truths that drift.
Do: Compute total, filtered list or label in the render body.
Don't: Mirror a derived value into state with an effect.
Code Good: const total = items.reduce((sum, it) => sum + it.price * it.qty, 0)

Guideline: Lift state to the nearest shared parent
Description: Two siblings that must agree should read one value owned by their closest common parent.
Do: Pass the value and its setter down as props.
Don't: Keep copies in both siblings and sync them.

Guideline: Use a reducer when updates share rules
Description: Several fields that change together, or many update paths, are easier to follow as named actions.
Do: Use useReducer with action names that read as events.
Don't: Call five setters in a row to express one change.

Description: State updates are queued; a function form reads the latest queued value.
Do: Pass an updater when the next value depends on the last.
Don't: Read the variable from the render and set it twice.

Description: React compares by identity; changing an object in place can leave the screen stale.
Do: Create a new object or array and set it.
Don't: Push into an array held in state.

Guideline: Reset a subtree with a key
Description: A different key makes React discard the old component state and start fresh.
Do: Key a form or profile panel by the record id.
Don't: Write an effect that clears each field when the id changes.

Guideline: Keep state structure flat and free of duplicates
Description: Nested copies of the same record must be updated in several places.
Do: Store ids in one place and look the record up.
Don't: Hold the selected object and the list it came from.

Guideline: Use context for rarely changing shared values
Description: Theme, locale and the signed-in user fit context; fast-changing values re-render every consumer.
Do: Split contexts by how often they change.
Don't: Put a typing buffer in a context everyone reads.

Guideline: Provide context as a component in 19
Description: React 19 lets the context object render as its own provider.
Do: Write the context directly as the wrapper.
Don't: Keep adding .Provider in new code.

Guideline: Effects are for syncing with outside systems
Description: Subscriptions, timers, and non-React widgets need an effect; reacting to a click does not.
Do: Do event work in the event handler.
Don't: Run a post request from an effect after a click flag flips.

Guideline: Always return a cleanup for subscriptions
Description: Without cleanup, listeners and timers pile up across re-renders and in StrictMode's double run.
Do: Return a function that undoes what the effect set up.
Don't: Add a listener and leave it attached.

Guideline: List every reactive value in the dependency array
Description: An omitted dependency makes the effect read stale values.
Do: Fix the code so the lint rule is quiet.
Don't: Silence the exhaustive-deps rule.

Guideline: Fetch with a guard against stale responses
Description: A slow earlier response can land after a newer one.
Do: Set an ignore flag in cleanup, or use a framework data layer.
Don't: Set state from whichever response arrives last.

Description: It keeps a store subscription consistent during concurrent rendering.
Do: Subscribe through the hook for browser or store state.
Don't: Copy store values into state inside an effect.

Guideline: Use useLayoutEffect only for measuring before paint
Description: It blocks the browser from painting; most effects do not need that.
Do: Measure a tooltip then place it, in a layout effect.
Don't: Use it for data loading.

Guideline: Use refs for values that do not drive the screen
Description: Timer ids and DOM nodes live in a ref; changing a ref does not re-render.
Do: Store ids and instances in useRef.
Don't: Read ref.current while rendering.

Guideline: Use a ref callback for node setup and teardown
Description: In 19 a ref callback can return a cleanup function.
Do: Return a cleanup from the callback.
Don't: Attach observers in an effect that queries the DOM by id.

Guideline: Pass ref as a prop in 19
Description: Function components receive ref as a normal prop, so forwardRef is no longer needed for new code.
Do: Read ref from props.
Don't: Wrap every component in forwardRef.

Description: Same props and state must give the same output, with no writes to outside values.
Do: Compute only from inputs.
Don't: Mutate a module variable or call Math.random for output.

Guideline: Use stable keys from the data
Description: Keys tell React which row is which; index keys break state when rows reorder.
Do: Use a database id.
Don't: Use array index for a list that can change.

Description: A component defined inside another is a new type every render and loses its state.
Do: Declare components at the top level.
Don't: Declare a component inside a render body.

Description: A bare number on the left of && prints on the page.
Do: Compare to produce a boolean.
Don't: Write count && <Badge/>.

Guideline: Return fragments instead of wrapper divs
Description: Extra wrappers break table, list and grid markup.
Do: Use <>...</> when no element is needed.
Don't: Wrap rows in a div inside a table.

Description: It double-runs renders and effects to expose impure code and missing cleanup.
Do: Keep StrictMode around the app root.
Don't: Remove it to hide a double-fire.

Description: memo, useMemo and useCallback have a cost and help only where renders are slow.
Do: Profile first, then memoize the hot spot.
Don't: Wrap every component in memo.

Guideline: Try the React Compiler before hand-memoizing
Description: The compiler memoizes automatically when code follows the rules of React.
Do: Enable the compiler and delete redundant memo calls.
Don't: Hand-memoize everything in a compiler project.

Guideline: Keep state close to where it is used
Description: State high in the tree re-renders everything below it on each keystroke.
Do: Move fast-changing state into a small child.
Don't: Store input text at the app root.
Code Bad: <App> holds q for the whole page

Guideline: Split code with lazy and Suspense
Description: Routes and heavy widgets need not ship in the first bundle.
Do: Lazy-load below-the-fold or route-level components.
Don't: Import a charting library on the landing page.

Description: The input stays responsive while an expensive list catches up.
Do: Defer the query that feeds the heavy list.
Don't: Debounce with timers by hand.

Description: startTransition keeps clicks and typing responsive while a tab or route switch renders.
Do: Wrap the slow state change.
Don't: Block the UI with a long synchronous render.

Description: Thousands of DOM nodes cost memory and layout time.
Do: Render only visible rows.
Don't: Map 10000 rows into the page.

Description: React DOM exposes preload and preconnect calls for fonts, scripts and images.
Do: Call preload for the hero image or font.
Don't: Wait for CSS to discover a late font.

Description: A function passed to action receives FormData and works with pending state.
Do: Pass a function to the form's action.
Don't: Write onSubmit with preventDefault for every form.

Description: A submit button inside the form can read whether it is sending.
Do: Disable the button and name the action while pending.
Don't: Allow double submits.

Description: The state returned from the action feeds messages back to the form.
Do: Return an errors object from the action.
Don't: Throw for expected validation failures.

Description: Show the expected result at once and fall back if the request fails.
Do: Add the pending item to the list instantly.
Don't: Make the user wait for the round trip.

Description: Placeholder text vanishes and is not a name for assistive tech (WCAG 2.2 SC 1.3.1, 3.3.2).
Do: Use a label tied with htmlFor and useId.
Don't: Use only a placeholder.

Guideline: Use the right input type and autocomplete
Description: Correct type and autocomplete tokens bring the right keyboard and autofill (WCAG 2.2 SC 1.3.5).
Do: Set type, inputMode and autoComplete.
Don't: Use type text for everything.

Description: Switching an input between controlled and uncontrolled logs warnings and loses values.
Do: Give value an initial string.
Don't: Start with undefined then set a value.

Guideline: Tell people about errors in text
Description: Colour alone is not enough (SC 1.4.1); announce errors near the field (SC 3.3.1).
Do: Link the message with aria-describedby and set aria-invalid.
Don't: Only turn the border red.

Guideline: Booking form: keep one clear primary action
Description: A booking or quote form converts when the fields are few and the button names the result.
Do: Ask name, phone, time; label the button Book a visit.
Don't: Add ten optional fields and a button labelled Submit.

Description: button, a, nav, main and headings carry roles and keyboard behaviour for free (SC 4.1.2).
Do: Use button for actions and a for navigation.
Don't: Attach onClick to a div.

Description: Focus must be visible (SC 2.4.7) and move sensibly after route or dialog changes.
Do: Move focus to the dialog or page heading with a ref.
Don't: Remove outlines globally.

Description: A tel link works for keyboard, screen readers and phones.
Do: Render an a element with tel: and the number as its text.
Don't: Use a button that sets window.location.

Description: Informative images need alt (SC 1.1.1); decoration gets empty alt.
Do: Write alt that says what the image shows.
Don't: Leave out alt or write 'image'.

Description: Users who ask for less motion should not get parallax or large slides (SC 2.3.3).
Do: Read the media query and skip the animation.
Don't: Animate regardless of the setting.

Guideline: Set the page title per view
Description: A unique title helps orientation (SC 2.4.2).
Do: Render <title> in the component; React hoists it.
Don't: Leave one static title for every route.

Description: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 asks for 24 by 24 CSS pixels at least; 44 is friendlier.
Do: Pad small icon buttons.
Don't: Pack 16px icons side by side.

Guideline: Use portals for dialogs but keep order
Description: createPortal renders outside the parent DOM; focus trap and labelling remain your job.
Do: Label the dialog and return focus on close.
Don't: Portal an unlabelled box.

Guideline: Read promises with use and Suspense
Description: use unwraps a promise passed from a server component, with Suspense for the wait.
Do: Pass the promise and wrap in Suspense.
Don't: Create the promise during client render.

Description: Boundaries let parts of the page appear as they load.
Do: Wrap slow sections with a skeleton fallback.
Don't: Block the whole page on one fetch.

Guideline: Catch render errors with a boundary
Description: An uncaught render error unmounts the tree; a boundary shows a fallback.
Do: Wrap risky sections in an error boundary.
Don't: Leave a blank page on failure.

Description: In server components cache avoids repeating the same read in one request.
Do: Wrap the loader in cache.
Don't: Fetch the same row in five components.

Description: Only files that need state, effects or events need use client.
Do: Mark leaf components as client.
Don't: Put use client at the top of the layout.

Guideline: Treat server functions as public endpoints
Description: A use server function can be called by any client; check auth and validate input inside it.
Do: Verify the session and parse input.
Don't: Trust arguments from the form.
Code Good: async function pay(fd){'use server'; await requireUser(); ...}

Guideline: Keep secrets and tokens off the client
Description: Anything in a client bundle is readable.
Do: Read secrets only in server code.
Don't: Put a secret key in a VITE_ or NEXT_PUBLIC_ variable.

Description: A hidden button is not access control.
Do: Check the session on the server for every protected read and write.
Don't: Only hide links when logged out.

Guideline: Stripe Checkout: create the session on the server
Description: A hosted checkout page keeps card data off your site; the price comes from your server.
Do: Create the session server-side and redirect to its url.
Don't: Send the amount from the browser.

Description: The success redirect can be skipped or faked; fulfil from a signed event.
Do: Verify the signature and fulfil on checkout.session.completed.
Don't: Mark an order paid on the success page load.

Guideline: Keep components idempotent for strict double renders
Description: Rendering twice must give the same result, or StrictMode reveals the bug.
Do: Move side effects to handlers and effects.
Don't: Increment a counter during render.

Description: React 19 hoists title, meta and link tags into the head.
Do: Place meta tags inside the page component.
Don't: Mutate document.head in an effect.

Description: The precedence prop lets React order and dedupe stylesheets and wait before reveal.
Do: Add href and precedence to link.
Don't: Inject style tags after first paint.

Guideline: Avoid server and client output mismatches
Description: Dates, random ids and window checks that differ between server and client break hydration.
Do: Render stable values; do browser-only work after mount.
Don't: Call Date.now() or window.innerWidth in render.

Description: useId gives the same id on server and client.
Do: Use it for label and aria links.
Don't: Use Math.random for ids.

Guideline: Give images dimensions and lazy loading
Description: Width and height prevent layout shift (CLS); lazy loading saves bytes.
Do: Set width, height, loading='lazy' below the fold.
Don't: Ship the hero as lazy; omit size.

Description: The largest image above the fold should not be lazy and can be preloaded.
Do: Use fetchPriority high on the one hero.
Don't: Mark every image high priority.

Description: Composing with children avoids a prop for every variation.
Do: Accept children in layout components.
Don't: Add boolean props for every layout variant.

Guideline: Do not copy props into state
Description: A prop copied into initial state ignores later updates.
Do: Use the prop directly, or reset with a key.
Don't: Initialise state from a prop that will change.

Description: If a parent must call focus or scroll, expose just those methods.
Do: Return a small object.
Don't: Hand the entire DOM node to the parent.
